solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bovine disease to catch, wife caught, then bovine

indicators.note: caught means the wife is held inside the word for catch

parts.note: to catch a criminal is to cop him, in slang
an ox is a bovine animal

explanation.surface: A farmer frets about cattle illness spreading through the household, wife included, then the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' puts W inside COP; 'to' and 'then' are link words. The second 'bovine' is a noun here, a beast of the cattle family.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild viral infection of cattle, once used to vaccinate people against smallpox, so it is an illness of cows.

clue.text: Note, a piece of music, and film musical

parts.note: C is a musical note
a bar is a short measure of music
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A list of things a film musical needs: a note, a tune and the movie itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word; 'film musical' looks like one phrase but 'film' is ET.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage show set in a Berlin nightclub, later filmed, is a famous musical by Kander and Ebb.

clue.text: Get item of luggage into new American camper

parts.note: to win something is to get it

indicators.note: into says the luggage goes inside the word for new

parts.note: neo- is a prefix meaning new
a bag is an item of luggage

explanation.surface: Instructions to stow a bag in a fresh American motorhome.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of large motorhome made in Iowa, so the name stands for an American camper van.

clue.text: Gooner's inebriate state

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An Arsenal supporter is described as being in a drunken condition.
explanation.walkthrough: A Gooner is a fan of Arsenal football club. 'inebriate' rearranges GOONER into the answer; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pacific Northwest member of the fifty United States, so it is an American state.

clue.text: New elastic bands made originally for plant

indicators.note: bands means wraps around, so the shuffled letters encircle the next piece
new suggests the word elastic is made over in fresh order
originally points to the first letter of the word made

explanation.surface: A gardener ties up a climbing plant with fresh elastic bands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges ELASTIC into CLEATIS, and 'bands' wraps that around M, the first letter of 'made' (signalled by 'originally').
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing flowering vine of the buttercup family, so it is a garden plant.

clue.text: Retreat where former PM is guillotined

indicators.note: guillotined means the head is cut off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Tony Blair was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A hideaway where an ex-Prime Minister meets a violent end.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was UK Prime Minister 1997-2007. 'guillotined' removes his head, the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A den or hideout where an animal or person withdraws is a retreat.

clue.text: Cut meals out, wanting drink

indicators.note: out suggests the words are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone skips food and reaches for a drink instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CUTMEALS; 'wanting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fortified wine made from muscat grapes is a drink.

clue.text: A dish from India cut up for the crown

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece is read from bottom to top
cut means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: raita is an Indian yoghurt side dish

explanation.surface: An Indian dish is chopped up to make a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims RAITA to RAIT, 'up' turns that to TIAR, and the opening A goes at the end. 'for the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, a type of crown or coronet.

clue.text: Anxious with the canonised J.R.?

parts.note: a canonised person is a saint, abbreviated ST
J.R. Ewing was the scheming oil baron of the TV soap Dallas

explanation.surface: A question whether being made a saint would make J.R. nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: J.R. Ewing was the villain of the American soap Dallas. 'with the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretting or worrying over something, as in 'still stewing about it', is being anxious.

clue.text: Meaty firework?

parts.note: a firework that is somehow made of meat: a noisy explosive and a British slang word for a sausage share one name

explanation.surface: A firework made of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a banger is a sausage as well as a loud firework.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang names a sausage this way, and it is also a loud exploding firework.

clue.text: Give a false impression of modern art's beauty queen?

parts.note: beauty pageant winners are titled Miss, as in Miss World
Tate Modern is London's gallery of modern art

explanation.surface: Asking who would be the beauty queen of a modern art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate Modern is a London gallery; a beauty queen is a 'Miss Somewhere', so the gallery's queen is MISS TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To state wrongly, giving people a false impression of the facts, is a verb meaning misrepresent.

clue.text: Colour seen by farmers on top of tractor

parts.note: pigmen are people who farm pigs

indicators.note: in a down clue, the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A colour visible to farmers sitting on a tractor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'seen by' are links; 'top of' takes T from 'tractor', placed after PIGMEN in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that gives colour to paint or tissue, so it stands for colour.

clue.text: Time to retire before erotic dancing becomes insincere stuff

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: HR is an abbreviation for hour, a unit of time

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters move about

explanation.surface: A suggestive dance is dismissed as empty talk.
explanation.walkthrough: HR, an hour, is the time; 'to retire' sends it backwards, and 'dancing' scrambles the next word. 'becomes' links wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Language meant to persuade or impress, often seen as empty or insincere talk.

clue.text: Vegetarian option not finished, Mudd's back for meat

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a salad is a meat-free choice on a menu

indicators.note: back means the contraction is read in reverse

parts.note: Mudd is the setter, so Mudd's means I'm

explanation.surface: A diner abandons the salad and the setter goes back for meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Mudd is the setter, so 'Mudd's' = I'M ('Mudd is' = 'I am'); 'back' turns it to MI. 'not finished' trims SALAD to SALA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cured Italian sausage, spiced and sliced, is a cooked meat.

clue.text: Shot at draw

parts.note: to draw someone in is to tempt them

explanation.surface: A shot taken at a drawn game.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a shot at something is making an attempt or try.

clue.text: National draw broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word's sound counts

parts.note: a draw in a match is a tie

explanation.surface: The national lottery draw is shown on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' looks like an adjective; here it is a noun for a citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Thailand is a national of that country.

clue.text: Carol consumes stuff for taste

indicators.note: consumes means swallows up, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: to carol is to sing
stuff as material is matter

explanation.surface: A carol singer is said to eat things for the taste of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight knowledge or small amount, a little taste of something.

clue.text: Nice to leave one under popular fish sauce

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
sole is a flatfish

indicators.note: to leave means the letter for one departs from the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Nice is the setting for a fish dish in a trendy sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city's name but serves as plain letters; 'to leave' drops the I. 'under' places that piece below the others in this down entry. 'Sauce' means cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce in the sense of cheeky impudence; insolence is rude disrespect.

clue.text: English city where bad spellers go

parts.note: witches cast wicked spells, and a coven is a gathering of them
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Joke that poor spellers are banished to a Midlands city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spellers' are those who cast spells, not who spell words. 'Sent to Coventry' is a British idiom for being shunned.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral city in the West Midlands of England.

clue.text: Said to be conspicuous

definitions.meaning: spoken or uttered aloud, as a word is
marked or very noticeable, as in a strong accent

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both articulated in speech and strikingly noticeable.

clue.text: Gasp, accepting resolution, as item suspended

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
the resolution of a story is its end

explanation.surface: A breathless moment as a decision is reached about something hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewel or ornament hanging from a chain, an item suspended round the neck.

clue.text: Old capitals of Sweden, Latvia and Oman — or another?

indicators.note: capitals means initial letters of the listed words

explanation.surface: Asking about former capital cities of three countries, or one more.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals are first letters, but 'another?' plays on capital cities: the answer is another capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway's capital city, one more capital besides those of the listed countries.

clue.text: People in boats, as circling river, passing through warning sign

indicators.note: passing through means sitting inside the warning sign word

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign

indicators.note: circling means going around, so the word as surrounds the next letter

explanation.surface: Boaters circle a river and pass an ominous sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts R inside the word 'as' to make ARS, and 'passing through' sets ARS within the warning sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers who propel boats with oars are people in boats.

clue.text: Secrets during war can appear

indicators.note: during means the answer occurs within the run of letters

explanation.surface: Secrets come out in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysteries or hidden knowledge known only to initiates, plural secrets.

clue.text: Food item in barrel knocked over, something valuable

indicators.note: knocked over means tipped up, so it reads backwards
in means the food item is placed inside the barrel

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel
an egg is an item of food

explanation.surface: Food inside a barrel that was tipped over turns out to be valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the food item inside the barrel to give TEGGUN, and 'knocked over' turns the whole thing backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump of gold, or figuratively a valuable piece of information.

clue.text: Fine sum of money

definitions.meaning: slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.definitionFit: The word means splendid, and is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.

clue.text: Gem of a firework?

definitions.meaning: slang for a diamond or sparkling jewel
a hand-held firework throwing off sparks

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a diamond, and the name of a hand-held firework.

clue.text: Orient's heading for relegation in rowdy game

indicators.note: relegation sends something to the bottom, so the letter moves to the end

parts.note: rowdy means loud

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Leyton Orient face relegation in a rowdy game.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a London football club; relegation drops a team down a league. Here the O at the head of LOUD drops to the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple board game with counters and dice for children.

clue.text: Plant a vessel just like that!

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel
thus means in this way, just like that

explanation.surface: A conjuror produces a plant from a pot, just like that.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean plant with spiny leaves, the model for Corinthian capitals.

clue.text: Arm with large bottle

definitions.meaning: a firearm, specifically a powerful revolver
a wine bottle holding twice the standard amount

explanation.definitionFit: A powerful revolver cartridge or gun, and a double-size wine bottle.

clue.text: Rocker died in body, yet resurrected

indicators.note: resurrected means raised again in new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rock musician dies but rises again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocker' suggests a rock musician or a chair, but a Teddy boy was a 1950s rock-and-roll youth. 'resurrected' rearranges D (died), BODY and YET; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1950s British youth subculture member in Edwardian dress, associated with rock and roll.

clue.text: Hostelry where bird stashes a number of gold rings

indicators.note: stashes means hides inside

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
five gold rings in the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas, V in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A bird hides golden rings where drinkers gather.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'The Twelve Days of Christmas' there are five gold rings; V is Roman five. 'where' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn or pub serving drinks is a hostelry.
